description: The pie chart visually represents the distribution of content categories across a dataset, likely used in the context of training or evaluating a multimodal large language model for video captioning. It is divided into 14 distinct slices, each labeled with a category and its corresponding percentage. The largest segment, colored orange, represents “People Blogs” at 17.2%. The second largest, in purple, is “Entertainment” at 13.9%, followed by “Education” in red at 8.7%, and “Howto Style” in green at 9.7%. Other categories include “Film Animation” (4.6%), “Sports” (7.7%), “Gaming” (6.4%), “Travel Events” (4.6%), “Comedy” (5.6%), “Science Technology” (6.4%), “News Politics” (4.3%), “Pets Animals” (3.9%), “Autos Vehicles” (4.8%), and “Music” (2.3%). The chart uses a color-coded legend implicitly through labeled slices, with no additional legend or exploded segments, and the slices are arranged in a roughly clockwise order starting from the top-right. Percentages are displayed inside each slice, allowing for direct comparison of category prevalence.
